title: What Is Revenue Leakage? Definition, Causes & How to Fix It
description: Revenue leakage explained: what it means, common causes across SaaS and ecommerce, and how to find leaks before they compound.

faq.q: What is revenue leakage in simple terms?
faq.a: Money you should have earned but did not — because something in your funnel (traffic, sales, billing, retention) failed, not because customers disappeared.

faq.q: Is revenue leakage illegal or fraud?
faq.a: Usually no. It is operational — slow follow-up, failed payments, cart abandonment, pricing errors — not theft.

faq.q: How is revenue leakage different from low revenue?
faq.a: Low revenue can mean weak demand. Leakage means demand or customers exist, but process gaps prevent you from capturing full value.

blocks.text: Revenue leakage is the gap between revenue you could collect and revenue you actually collect. The customer may still be interested, the product may still deliver value, but a broken step — slow demo follow-up, a declined card, an abandoned cart — lets money escape.

items: Acquisition: traffic that never becomes a qualified lead
Response: leads that go cold before anyone replies
Conversion: trials, demos, or carts that stall before payment
Retention: customers who churn early or never activate
Billing: failed payments, invoice delays, pricing drift
Expansion: customers who would upgrade but never see an offer

blocks.text: See [revenue leakage examples](/blog/revenue-leakage-examples) for worked patterns by business type.
